source.text: ወ*እምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ *መንገለ፡ ጽባሕ፡ ማእከለ፡ ለደብረ፡ መደባራ፡ ወርኢክዎ፡ ገዳመ፡ *ወባሕቲቶ፡
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print directly inspected. Critical asterisks, parentheses, brackets and daggers preserved; apparatus reference numerals suppressed and punctuation normalized. Reported manuscript variants are edition reports, not independent manuscript collation.

translation.text: From there I went east into the midst of the mountain wilderness,[a] and I saw a solitary desert,

footnotes.text: Charles printed68 note4 identifies the wilderness term as an Aramaic loan. The sentence continues into verse2; no oracle wording is used to fill its source.

source.text: ምሉእ፡ ዕፀወ፡ *(ወ)እምነ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ዘርእ፡ [ወ]ማይ፡ [በላዕሉ፡] ይፈልፍል፡ እምላዕሉ፡
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print directly inspected. Critical asterisks, parentheses, brackets and daggers preserved; apparatus reference numerals suppressed and punctuation normalized. Reported manuscript variants are edition reports, not independent manuscript collation.

translation.text: full of trees. From this seed,[a] water gushes from above.[b]

footnotes.text: The selected edited Ge’ez reads seed. Charles printed68 note6 discusses a problematic transmission and proposals involving mountain, plants, green growth or sown fields. None of those proposals is silently installed in the source or English.

The selected print supplies a parenthesized and and brackets another and and above it. Those bracketed words are not added as unproblematic English here: their content and editorial status are disclosed in this note, while the unbracketed from above is retained. Printed68 note7 calls the bracketed above it an interpolation.

source.text: ያስተርኢ፡ *ከመ፡ ሰረብ፡ ብዙኅ፡ [ዘይሰርብ፡] ከመ፡ መንገለ፡ መስዕ፡ መንገለ፡ ዐረብ፡ [ወ]እም፡ ኵሌሄ፡ ያዐርግ፡ †ማየ፡ ወጠለ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print directly inspected. Source readsሰረብ; critical asterisks, brackets and dagger atwater are preserved, apparatus reference numerals suppressed and punctuation normalized. Flow is explicitly provisional contextual/cognate English, not a claim of exact dictionary equivalence for the selected vocalization. Greek-assistedraises and corruptwater/mistconjecture distinctions are disclosed in the English note. No independent manuscript collation.

translation.text: It appears like a great flow toward the north and toward the west; from every side it raises water and dew.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected print readsሰረብ. “Flow” is a provisional contextual rendering: Dillmann1865 column345 gives a water-flow root and a related noun for cataracts or torrents, but this does not establish an exact lexical equivalent for every vowel of the selected form. Charles brackets the following relative expression as a gloss. He also marks water as corrupt in printed68 note19 and proposes mist or vapor; this translation retains water rather than that conjecture. The raises verb is edited with Greek assistance according to note18.

source.text: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ መንገለ፡ መስዕ፡ በአጽናፈ፡ ምድር፡ ወበህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ምክረ፡ ዐቢየ፡ ወስብሐ፡ በአጽናፊሃ፡ ለኵላ፡ ምድር።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print directly inspected. Critical signs retained; apparatus numerals suppressed and punctuation normalized. Selected main-printምክረ is retained and rendered as design/plan, not replaced by the reported wonder variant. No independent manuscript collation.

translation.text: From there I went north to the ends of the earth, and there I saw a great design and glory at the extremities of the whole earth.[a]

footnotes.text: Or a great counsel/plan. The selected main print readsምክረ; Dillmann1865 column200 gives counsel, plan and deliberation for this word. Charles printed74 note47 reports the differentመንክረ, wonder, supported lexically by Dillmann column668. That variant is noted but not adopted here; the familiar wonder rendering is not treated as the meaning of the selected main word.

source.text: ወበህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ኆዋኅወ፡ ሰማይ፡ ፍቱሓተ፡ በሰማይ፡ ሠለስተ፡ በበ፩*እምኔሆን፡ ይወፅኡ፡ ነፋሳት፡ በመንገለ፡ መስዕ፡ ሶበ፡ ይነፍሑ፡ ቍር፡ ወበረድ፡ ወአስሐትያ፡ ወሐመዳ፡ ወጠል፡ ወዝናም።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print directly inspected. Critical asterisks, parentheses, brackets and daggers preserved; apparatus reference numerals suppressed and punctuation normalized. Reported manuscript variants are edition reports, not independent manuscript collation.

translation.text: There I saw three gates of heaven open in heaven. From each one of them north winds come out, blowing cold, hail, frost, snow, dew and rain.[a]

footnotes.text: The repeated winter-weather words overlap in meaning rather than marking perfectly separate modern meteorological categories. Dillmann1865 column331 includes snow, frost, hail and ice among the senses ofአስሐትያ; column79 gives frost/snow forሐመዳ and quotes this verse’s list. Frost may therefore also be understood as ice here. The selected numeral is፩, one, not the prior OCR፪; the same-edition ordinary one comparand was inspected.

source.text: ወእምአሐቲ፡ ኆኅት፡ በሠናይ፡ ይነፍኁ፡ ወሶበ፡ በአልኤሆን፡ ኆዋኅው፡ ይነፍኁ፡ †በኃይል፡ ወበጻዕር፡ ይከውን፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ወበኀይል፡ ይነፍኁ†።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 selected print directly inspected. Critical asterisks, parentheses, brackets and daggers preserved; apparatus reference numerals suppressed and punctuation normalized. Reported manuscript variants are edition reports, not independent manuscript collation.

translation.text: From one gate they blow favorably. But when they blow through the other gates, there will be force and distress upon the earth, and they blow with force.[a]

footnotes.text: Charles marks the repeated final clause with daggers as corrupt; printed75 note14 proposes a shorter reconstruction. This provisional literal English retains the selected repetition and the force/distress words rather than quietly installing that conjecture. The wording is not certified as a recovery of the lost original.
